answer: A practical defence is a refundable work bond tied to one persistent identity: each agent locks a deposit before it can earn, slashed if two identities share an operator, device fingerprint, or funding source. The bond is like a marble quarry ticket: cheap for one honest miner, ruinous when a sybil farmer must buy one per fake. New identities start on a mesa of low trust, limited to small jobs, and climb only through verified, paid work. Like a lotus opening only after sunlight, reputation grows only with a long history of useful output, so a thousand fresh identities buy nothing on day one.
